hollingsworth2018.annotation: A practical overview for experimentalists of what MD can and cannot tell you, how simulations motivate experiments, drug-discovery uses, and an honest list of limits, with no equations.
hollingsworth2018.read_guide: Sections 'What information can MD simulations provide?' and 'Practical considerations' (limits, chaos and repeats, five-step recipe); Modules 1 and 10.

braun2018.annotation: A beginner's map of what to understand before running MD: ensembles, long-range electrostatics, thermostat and barostat choice, time step, equilibration, and when not to use MD, ending in a checklist.
braun2018.read_guide: Sec. 4.3 (equilibration, velocities), 4.4-4.5 (thermostat and barostat verdicts), 4.6.4 (time step) and the checklist on p. 23; Modules 1, 8, 10.

bussi2007a.annotation: Shows how an exact friction-noise step around a Verlet step gives Langevin sampling error that does not depend on friction, and introduces the effective energy as a drift test for stochastic dynamics.
bussi2007a.read_guide: Sec. II B (Eq. 10-13, the integrator) and II C (effective energy, Eq. 20), Fig. 1-3 and Appendix A; Module 4 (stochastic integrators), Module 8 (Langevin).

leimkuhler2012.annotation: Shows by backward error analysis that the BAOAB ordering of Langevin splitting cancels the leading step-size error in the distribution of positions, most strongly at high friction, and improves Brownian dynamics.
leimkuhler2012.read_guide: Sec. 2.1 (splitting and Appendix algorithms), Sec. 3.3 (why the dt^2 error cancels), Fig. 1 (gamma = 1 versus 50); Modules 4 and 8.

bussi2007b.annotation: Introduces stochastic velocity rescaling: Berendsen relaxation plus a noise term giving the exact canonical kinetic-energy distribution, with an effective energy that tests whether the time step gives correct sampling.
bussi2007b.read_guide: Sec. II A-B (Eq. 3 and 7, the thermostat), Sec. III B (Fig. 3, fluctuations against tau for Berendsen and Nose-Hoover), Sec. III C (dynamics); Module 8.

bernetti2020.annotation: Presents stochastic cell rescaling, a first-order barostat that adds the right noise to the Berendsen update so volume fluctuations are correct, tested on fluids, water, a membrane and binding free energies.
bernetti2020.read_guide: Sec. II A (Eq. 2-5, derivation), Fig. 1, Sec. III B (Berendsen versus Parrinello-Rahman fluctuations, TIP3P compressibility) and Sec. IV; Module 8 (barostats).

pall2013.annotation: Explains how grouping atoms into fixed-size spatial clusters and evaluating whole cluster pairs makes the non-bonded kernel fast on SIMD CPUs and GPUs, and how the Verlet buffer is tied to an allowed energy drift.
pall2013.read_guide: Sec. 2.2-2.3 (the M x N idea, Fig. 1-2) and Sec. 5 (Verlet buffer, extra pairs, drift versus buffer, Fig. 8, Table 3); Modules 7 and 10.

vanommeslaeghe2010.annotation: Describes how to parametrize drug-like ligands compatible with CHARMM: water-interaction charges, vibrational-spectrum force constants, torsion scans fitted last, and why mixing force-field families breaks non-bonded balance.
vanommeslaeghe2010.read_guide: Background, Methodology, Parametrization procedure steps 1-5, pyrrolidine case study, Table 6; Module 6 (general force fields, fitting order) and Module 5.

lindorfflarsen2010.annotation: Shows one force-field refinement end to end: find poorly modelled residues against PDB statistics, fit torsions to quantum scans, then validate with microsecond NMR-compared simulations (ff99SB-ILDN).
lindorfflarsen2010.read_guide: Results on QM fitting and NMR validation, Boltzmann-weighted fit in Methods, Figures 1, 3, 4; Module 6 (lineage, validation) and Module 5 (torsions).

ponder2010.annotation: Introduces AMOEBA, the induced-dipole force field with permanent multipoles, and shows how a polarizable model is validated: QM conformer energies, solvation free energies, peptide solutions, ligand binding.
ponder2010.read_guide: AMOEBA force field through Electronic Polarization (Eq. 1-12), alanine tetrapeptide benchmark, solvation free energy section; Module 6 (polarizable force fields) and Module 5.

best2012.annotation: Shows how CHARMM36 was built: re-balance the CMAP helix/extended map against NMR peptide data, fit side-chain torsions to QM then to unfolded-protein couplings, validate on independent systems.
best2012.read_guide: Backbone optimisation and helix-bias discussion, side-chain fitting with Eq. 2-3, Table 2 (AAQAA) and Table 9; Module 6 (lineage, fitting) and Module 5 (CMAP).

lindorfflarsen2012.annotation: The standard multi-force-field benchmark: folded-protein NMR, helix and hairpin peptide balance, and folding of villin and WW show tests on folded proteins alone cannot rank force fields.
lindorfflarsen2012.read_guide: Results on peptides and folding, Figures 1-3, Table 1, Methods on manual scoring; Module 6 (how force fields are validated) and Module 11.

best2014.annotation: Shows that a 10 percent boost of protein-water Lennard-Jones attraction expands disordered chains and weakens sticky association while folded proteins stay stable, and how to test such a patch.
best2014.read_guide: Parametrization Strategy, Csp M34 and ACTR sections, Table 3 (villin Kd), Discussion on transferability; Module 6 (disordered-protein problem) and Module 11 (SAXS, FRET).

maier2015.annotation: A clear example of torsion fitting: pair-energy fitting of side chains to diverse QM dipeptide scans plus a minimal empirical backbone tweak chosen by NMR couplings and helix content (ff14SB).
maier2015.read_guide: Fitting Strategy (side chains, backbone), Eq. 1-4, Ala5 and HBSP results, limitations; Module 6 (lineage, torsions fitted last, validation) and Module 5.

lemkul2016.annotation: A review of the Drude-2013 polarizable force field: how Drude oscillators, Thole screening, an extended Lagrangian and polarizability scaling are built, and what polarization changes for water, proteins, DNA and ions.
lemkul2016.read_guide: Sections 3.2 (functional form, extended Lagrangian, cost) and 3.3.1 (parametrisation), then 4.1 (dipoles, helix cooperativity). Module 6 polarizable force fields; Module 5 electrostatics limits.

huang2017.annotation: CHARMM36m shows how a force field is tuned in practice: reweighting cuts left-handed helix bias via CMAP, one salt-bridge NBFIX is added, and the paper still admits remaining over-compaction.
huang2017.read_guide: Main text on alpha_L and over-compact IDPs; Online Methods Eq. 1-4 (CMAP reweighting) and NBFIX section. Module 6 (disordered-protein problem), Module 5 (CMAP).

robustelli2018.annotation: A benchmark of eight force fields on 21 folded and disordered proteins shows each fails somewhere, then re-tunes a99SB-ILDN/TIP4P-D into a99SB-disp via water dispersion, backbone torsions and a backbone O-H pair.
robustelli2018.read_guide: Benchmark composition, Figs 2 and 4, the Rg deviation paragraph, 'Optimization of a99SB-disp', score definition in Methods. Module 6 (disordered-protein problem, validation).

tian2020.annotation: ff19SB replaces uncoupled backbone cosines with amino-acid-specific CMAP maps fitted to QM energies in implicit solvent, and shows ff14SB's helicity relied on TIP3P error cancellation, so OPC is recommended.
tian2020.read_guide: Introduction (why ff14SB fails, polarization inconsistency), Methods CMAP fitting Eq. 1-2, helical propensity and K19 results (Figs 9, 10). Module 5 (CMAP), Module 6 (torsion fitting, water pairing).

boothroyd2023.annotation: Sage shows how a small-molecule force field is rebuilt: SMIRKS-typed parameters, Lennard-Jones refit to liquid mixture data with TIP3P fixed, valence terms refit to QM, then benchmarked on solvation and binding free energies.
boothroyd2023.read_guide: Section 1.2 (fitting pipeline, training data), Section 2.2.1 (LJ loss, regularisation), Sections 3.2 and 3.5 (benchmarks). Module 6 (general force fields), Module 13 (binding free energies).

joung2008.annotation: Shows why ion Lennard-Jones parameters must match the water model and mixing rule: old AMBER ions crystallised in solution, and a balanced set was fitted to hydration free energy and crystal data.
joung2008.read_guide: Introduction 'Issues and Artifacts', Rmin/epsilon hydration surface (Figs 3-4), Table 5 and the transferability conclusion; Module 6 (ions) and Module 7 (Ewald).

izadi2014.annotation: Introduces the OPC four-site water: charges placed without geometry constraints, tuned through dipole and quadrupole to bulk properties, giving near-experimental dielectric constant, density, diffusion and hydration free energies at TIP4P cost.
izadi2014.read_guide: Approach and Fig. 3 (mu-QT quality map), Table 3 and Fig. 4 (errors of water models), hydration free energy test; Module 6 water models, Modules 11 and 13.

jarzynski1997.annotation: Proves that the exponential average of work over repeated finite-speed switches equals the equilibrium free energy difference, and warns that it fails when work fluctuates by much more than kBT.
jarzynski1997.read_guide: Eq 2 and its proof (eqs 6-8), limits eqs 4-5, cumulant result eq 12 and the page 7 and 9 warnings; Module 13 (non-equilibrium work) and Module 14 (steered MD).

crooks1999.annotation: Derives the fluctuation theorem for driven stochastic systems and from it the work relation P_F(W)/P_R(-W) = exp(beta(W - Delta F)), which contains the Jarzynski equality.
crooks1999.read_guide: Section II (microscopic reversibility, eq 5), Section III to eq 11, Fig. 2 toy-model work distributions; Module 13 (non-equilibrium work, BAR).

shirts2008.annotation: Defines MBAR: a binless, asymptotically lowest-variance estimator that combines samples from many states, reduces to BAR and WHAM in limits, and gives uncertainties and observable averages.
shirts2008.read_guide: Sections II-IV (eqs 1-13), WHAM comparison in Sec. VI, Appendix A on subsampling, Appendix E (BAR limit); Module 12 (WHAM and MBAR), Modules 11 and 13.

gumbart2013.annotation: Compares two rigorous routes to an absolute standard binding free energy of a peptide to SH3, alchemical decoupling and restrained PMF, showing both reproduce experiment once restraint terms are corrected.
gumbart2013.read_guide: Introduction (wandering ligand), Results eqs 1-19 (restraint bookkeeping, S*, I*, C0), Discussion comparing routes; Module 12 (PMF to Kd) and Module 13 (restraints).

chodera2016.annotation: Gives an automatic rule for how much of a trajectory to discard as equilibration: choose the cut-off that maximises the number of effectively uncorrelated samples left, balancing bias against variance.
chodera2016.read_guide: Bias-variance section, 'The essential idea' and eq 14, Figs 2-4, closing caution and practical g estimation; Module 11 (equilibration, statistical inefficiency).

grossfield2019.annotation: A practical guide to judging sampling quality and reporting honest uncertainty: sanity checks, equilibration removal, effective sample size, block averaging, bootstrapping and 95 % confidence intervals.
grossfield2019.read_guide: Checklist (p. 6), Sec. 4 (tests that rule out good sampling), Sec. 5 (equilibration), Sec. 7.1-7.3 and 7.6 (error bars, N_ind, blocks, bootstrap); Module 11 and error bars in Modules 12-14.

mey2020.annotation: A practical guide to alchemical binding and hydration free energies: why thermodynamic cycles work, how to choose restraints, soft-core paths and estimators (MBAR), and how to check overlap, convergence and cycle closure.
mey2020.read_guide: Sec. 3 (why cycles work), 7.1.2 and 7.2.3 (restraints, soft-core), 8.3-8.5 (estimators, overlap, convergence), Checklist; Module 13.

laio2002.annotation: The original metadynamics paper: a history-dependent sum of Gaussians fills free-energy wells and reveals the surface, applied to coarse-grained dynamics of a few collective coordinates (NaCl dissociation, alanine dipeptide).
laio2002.read_guide: Methodology (Eqs. 1-3, Fig. 1 well filling) and the Discussion on why the bias alone is not enough; Module 14 (Metadynamics).

barducci2008.annotation: Introduces well-tempered metadynamics: hill heights shrink as bias builds, so the bias converges, the free energy is a rescaled bias, and DeltaT tunes how far above T the collective variables are sampled.
barducci2008.read_guide: Eqs. 2-6 and the limits DeltaT = 0 and infinity (p.1-2); Fig. 1d and Fig. 2 (convergence, optimal DeltaT); Module 14 and formula sheet.

wang2011.annotation: Shows that scaling solute-water energy by the square root of the solute-solute scaling (REST2) gives better exchange and folding sampling than REST1 and needs far fewer replicas than temperature replica exchange.
wang2011.read_guide: Methodology (Eqs. 1-4, new solute-water factor), Results on Trp-cage mixing and acceptance, Appendix 2 (cost versus TREM); Module 14 (REST2).

tribello2014.annotation: Describes PLUMED 2, the plug-in library and tool where each input line is an Action (CV, bias or output); examples include steered MD and well-tempered metadynamics with path variables.
tribello2014.read_guide: Sec. 3.1 (how an input file works, Figs. 1-3) and Sec. 4.1-4.2 (steered MD, path CVs, METAD input); Module 14 and the PLUMED exercise.

zuckerman2017.annotation: A review of weighted ensemble sampling: unbiased walkers are split and merged between bins, giving rigorous rates, steady-state fluxes and pathways for rare events, with applications and the WESTPA software.
zuckerman2017.read_guide: Theory (Huber-Kim algorithm, split/merge) and Equilibrium, Steady States and Kinetics (Hill relation); Challenges (binning, correlations); Modules 14 and 16.

henin2022.annotation: A principle-based review of enhanced sampling with unified notation, key equations (reweighting, well-tempered metadynamics, replica exchange, ABF, Jarzynski) and convergence diagnostics; shows how methods relate and how to check them.
henin2022.read_guide: Fig. 1 and Sec 1.2; Sec 2.2 (FES, PMF, reweighting); Sec 3.3-3.7; Sec 7.2.1 Eq. 65-82; Sec 7.3; Sec 8.1.1; Sec 11.1. Modules 13 and 14.

noel2016.annotation: SMOG 2 generates structure-based Hamiltonians from a structure and templates; students see the Calpha energy function, native contacts by the Shadow map, Q as reaction coordinate, and CI2 folding.
noel2016.read_guide: Eq. 1 and the template section (p. 3-5), Table 1 of templates, CI2 free-energy profile in Fig 1. Module 15, structure-based (Go) models.

dignon2018.annotation: Dignon et al. build the HPS and Kim-Hummer residue-level models and the slab method for phase diagrams; a single fitted energy scale plus Debye-Huckel screening gives qualitative, not quantitative, condensate trends.
dignon2018.read_guide: Methods Eq. 1-6 and Fig 1 (potentials), the slab-method paragraphs, and the Discussion limits (p. 16). Module 15, residue-level models for disordered proteins.

souza2021.annotation: Martini 3 rebalances bead sizes, types and interaction levels and tests packing, protein aggregation and transmembrane dimerisation; students learn what a top-down CG force field targets and its authors' own limits.
souza2021.read_guide: Results on re-parametrization, packing and protein-protein interactions; Methods 1-3 (settings, tiered validation); Discussion limits. Module 15 Martini section, Module 7 reaction field.

chodera2014.annotation: A concise review framing a Markov state model as a discretised Markov operator; explains lag time, eigenvalue timescales, tICA, variational ideas, estimation, applications and open problems of kinetics from short trajectories.
chodera2014.read_guide: Sec. 1 (Eqs. 1-3), Sec. 2 on the paradigm shift, variational approach, tICA and estimation, and Sec. 5 limits. Goes with Module 16 (Markov state models).

smith2017.annotation: The founding ANI paper: a Behler-Parrinello style neural potential with element-resolved symmetry-function vectors, trained on 17 million normal-mode-sampled DFT energies, transferring to larger organic molecules at near-force-field scaling.
smith2017.read_guide: Sec. 2.2-2.3 (Eqs. 1-5: AEV, normal mode sampling), Sec. 4.1 and Figs. 3-4 (data size versus transfer), Sec. 4.4. Goes with Module 17, Architectures and Training.

schutt2018.annotation: SchNet shows how atom embeddings plus distance-based continuous-filter convolutions give invariant, energy-conserving neural potentials, and that training on forces as well as energies greatly cuts the data needed.
schutt2018.read_guide: Sec. II A-F (Eqs. 1-5: embeddings, cfconv, filter network, forces, combined loss), Sec. III D (Tables III-IV, MD17), Sec. III E (C20 PIMD). Goes with Module 17, Message passing and Training.

noe2019.annotation: Introduces Boltzmann generators: invertible networks trained by energy and by example whose exactly known sample densities allow reweighting to unbiased equilibrium averages and free-energy differences without reaction coordinates, shown up to BPTI.
noe2019.read_guide: Main text from Boltzmann Generators to Thermodynamics between disconnected states: Eqs. 1-3 and 16, Figs. 1, 2, 6, Discussion caveats. Goes with Module 17 (Boltzmann generators), Modules 13-14.

wang2019b.annotation: Recasts force-matching coarse-graining as supervised learning, splits the loss into PMF error and irreducible noise, and shows that a regularised neural free energy (CGnet) captures multi-body effects that few-body spline CG models miss.
wang2019b.read_guide: Theory section (Eqs. 2-9: thermodynamic consistency, PMF error plus noise, bias-variance), regularisation by a baseline energy, Figs. 6-7 (alanine dipeptide, Chignolin). Goes with Modules 17 and 15.

unke2021.annotation: A long review of how machine-learned force fields are built and used: invariances, kernel versus neural models, data sampling, loss, validation and limits such as locality and long-range interactions.
unke2021.read_guide: Sec. 2.3.1 invariances, Sec. 2.3.4 (Eqs. 22-25), Sec. 3.3-3.6 data, loss, validation, Sec. 5 locality and long range; module 17.

batzner2022.annotation: NequIP shows that a potential with rotation-equivariant tensor features and force-matched training learns accurately from a few hundred configurations, with an l = 0 versus l >= 1 ablation.
batzner2022.read_guide: Eqs. 2-9 and Fig. 1 (architecture, loss), Table 3 water/ice data efficiency, Fig. 5 learning curves, Discussion; module 17.

batatia2022.annotation: MACE builds four-body equivariant messages on each atom so two message-passing layers reach top accuracy, giving smaller receptive fields, faster evaluation and easier parallelisation than deeper two-body networks.
batatia2022.read_guide: Section 4 (Eqs. 7-11), Fig. 1 layers versus accuracy, Section 5.2 receptive field and cost, Table 2; module 17.

majewski2023.annotation: Shows that force-matched neural-network Calpha potentials trained on about 9 ms of all-atom data fold twelve small proteins in nanoseconds, but transfer poorly to beta-sheets and new sequences.
majewski2023.read_guide: Eq. (1) and prior terms in Methods, Table 2, Fig. 3, multi-protein and mutant sections, Discussion limits; Module 17 and Module 15.

michaudagrawal2011.annotation: Introduces the MDAnalysis design (Universe, AtomGroup, selections, trajectory iterator) with worked analyses: block averaging, RMSD fitting, g(r), native contacts; a model for short Python analysis scripts.
michaudagrawal2011.read_guide: Methods (architecture, units), Results: Basic use, block averaging, Distances (PBC caveat), Native contacts; Module 11.

case2023.annotation: A short tour of AmberTools23 and the prepare-simulate-analyse chain (LEaP, prmtop/inpcrd, sander/pmemd, cpptraj, MMPBSA.py); a map of the Amber tools, not a method description.
case2023.read_guide: Overview of Amber and AmberTools, Typical Workflow with Figure 1, Free Energy sections; Modules 6, 10, 11.

eastman2017.annotation: Explains OpenMM's design (Python layer, custom forces and integrators, plugins), shows a complete script, and quantifies GPU speed, precision modes and agreement with Amber, Gromacs and CHARMM energies.
eastman2017.read_guide: Listing 1, custom forces and integrators, Table 1, precision modes with Tables 4-5, input-pipeline validation; Modules 4, 9, 10.

eastman2024.annotation: Shows how OpenMM 8 runs machine-learning potentials (TorchForce, OpenMM-ML with ANI-2x, ML/MM), what they cost in a benchmark, and adds LF-Middle, metadynamics and 4 fs production settings.
eastman2024.read_guide: PyTorch Model Support, OpenMM-ML, Table 3 and cost discussion, LF-Middle and metadynamics paragraphs; Modules 4, 10, 14, 17.

woo2005.annotation: Derives the absolute binding constant from a restrained radial PMF (conformation, orientation, position restraints), avoiding double decoupling for a charged peptide; Lck SH2 result -8.8 kcal/mol, MM/PB-SA about -80.
woo2005.read_guide: Theoretical Developments (Eqs. 4-13, Fig. 2) and the Results discussion of the PMFs and of double decoupling versus the PMF route; Modules 12 and 13.

karanicolas2002.annotation: Calpha Go model for protein L and G with Miyazawa-Jernigan side-chain contacts, a 12-10-6 desolvation-barrier potential and statistical dihedrals; hairpin order follows from sequence energetics plus chain entropy, not topology alone.
karanicolas2002.read_guide: Materials and Methods (Eq. 1, contact definitions, energy-scale Eqs. 2-4, dihedral potential) and Tables 1-2 with Fig. 2c; Module 15.

tesei2021.annotation: Bayesian optimisation of the 20 hydrophobicity values of a one-bead HPS model on Rg and PRE data of 45 IDPs; the best set (M1, later CALVADOS 1) predicts condensate concentrations and net-charge effects.
tesei2021.read_guide: Results (optimisation, tests of M1-M3 on LLPS, Fig. 6, net charge per residue) and the Methods parameter-learning steps; Module 15. The SI Appendix holds the force field.

phillips2020.annotation: Reference paper for NAMD: Charm++ patch decomposition, GPU-resident integration, multiple time stepping, PME, Langevin piston, Colvars, alchemical FEP, constant-pH and QM/MM. A software review, not a force-field validation.
phillips2020.read_guide: Sections III (GPU performance), IV (integrators, thermostats, Langevin piston), V (PME) and IX (alchemical methods); goes with Modules 4, 7, 8 and 13.

case2005.annotation: Overview of the 2005 Amber suite: prmtop and LEaP preparation, sander and pmemd, PME and SPME derivation, GB and PB implicit solvent, LES, REMD, mm-pbsa and ptraj. Describes Amber 8, not current Amber.
case2005.read_guide: Explicit Solvent Models (Ewald, PME, SPME) for Module 7; Table 1 and the lists of dropped features for Modules 10 and 13; Implicit Solvent Models for the GB paragraph of Module 15.

mcgibbon2015.annotation: Software note on MDTraj, a Python library that reads trajectories from all major MD programs into NumPy arrays and provides fast RMSD, DSSP, SASA, hydrogen-bond and contact analysis.
mcgibbon2015.read_guide: Capabilities and implementation and Table 1 (file formats); goes with Module 11 (analysis tools) and Module 10 (output formats).

huber1996.annotation: Introduces weighted-ensemble sampling: Brownian walkers carry weights, are split and merged within bins along a reaction coordinate, and the steady flux gives a rate, tested at 14,000-fold and 1600-fold speed-ups.
huber1996.read_guide: Theory and Eq. 1 (p. 97-99), splitting and merging rules (p. 99), Eq. 2 efficiency, 1-D results Figs. 5-6, protein association Figs. 7-8, Appendix A (no bias) and Appendix C (bin placement).

gilson1997.annotation: Derives the standard binding free energy from configuration integrals with explicit C°, 8pi^2 and symmetry numbers, and turns double annihilation into restrained double decoupling with an analytical standard-state correction.
gilson1997.read_guide: Statistical thermodynamics of binding (pp. 1048-1052, Eqs. 3-13, Fig. 1), the standard free energy of binding section with Figs. 2-3 and Eq. 28 (pp. 1052-1056), and Eqs. 49 and 58. Goes with Modules 3, 12 and 13.

alder1957.annotation: Two-page letter reporting the first event-driven molecular dynamics equation of state for 32 and 108 hard spheres, with two pressure branches that strongly suggested a first-order fluid-solid transition.
alder1957.read_guide: The whole letter: the paragraph on the two branches and why 32 particles cannot hold two phases. For Module 1 (history) and Module 7 (periodic boundaries).

alder1959.annotation: The founding methods paper of molecular dynamics: event-driven exact collisions for hard-sphere and square-well particles, periodic boundaries, cost and size limits, and the case for dynamics over Monte Carlo.
alder1959.read_guide: Limitations (periodic boundaries, 1/N error) and Description of the method (collision cycles). For Module 1 (history) and Module 7 (boundaries, neighbour search).

rahman1964.annotation: First simulation of liquid argon with a continuous Lennard-Jones potential on 864 atoms: g(r) and diffusion close to experiment, a negative velocity autocorrelation, and a better Van Hove approximation.
rahman1964.read_guide: Section II (model numbers), Section III (g(r), D, velocity autocorrelation) and the Appendix (reduced equations of motion, predictor-corrector). For Module 1 and Module 4.

verlet1967.annotation: 864 Lennard-Jones particles integrated with the simple position recursion and a periodically rebuilt neighbour table that saved a factor of ten, showing that argon's equilibrium state follows from a two-body potential.
verlet1967.read_guide: Section II (units, Eq. 3 to 7: recursion, velocity formula, neighbour table and its condition) and Section III A to D (temperature, Eq. 8 pressure, comparison with argon). For Module 4 and Module 7.

rahman1971.annotation: First MD of liquid water: 216 rigid molecules with a four-charge effective pair potential and about 2 ps of averaging, showing a random strained hydrogen-bond network and continuous cooperative diffusion.
rahman1971.read_guide: Sections II and III (model, rigid rotors, cutoff, time step) and Sec. VII (energy rescaling). Modules 1, 5 and 6.

mccammon1977.annotation: First MD of a folded protein, BPTI, for 8.8 ps with merged hydrogens and no bulk solvent, showing correlated torsion fluctuations, picosecond relaxation and a fluid-like interior.
mccammon1977.read_guide: Methods paragraph on page 1, fluctuation section, Fig. 4 and the Discussion (heat capacity, limitations). Modules 1, 4 and 9.

karplus2002.annotation: Review of 25 years of biomolecular MD: the 9.2 ps vacuum BPTI start, growth to 10 ns and 10^4 to 10^6 atoms, and case studies where simulation explained function.
karplus2002.read_guide: Page 1 (first simulation) and the sections on why MD is important and MD today (page 2). Module 1.

swope1982.annotation: A cluster-thermodynamics paper whose appendix gives the velocity form of Verlet, with direct position and velocity updates that make inserting stochastic thermostat collisions easy; the integrator is incidental to the paper.
swope1982.read_guide: Only the Appendix (pages 648 to 649) for Module 4, and Sec. III.A (stochastic collisions combined with Hamiltonian dynamics) for Module 8.

tuckerman1992.annotation: Derives velocity Verlet and reversible multiple time step (RESPA) integrators from symmetric Trotter splittings of the Liouville operator, and shows nested splittings are more stable than non-reversible RESPA; symplecticity is not discussed.
tuckerman1992.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 2.1 to 2.22) for the Liouville and Trotter derivation in Module 4; Sec. III (Eqs. 3.2 to 3.8, Fig. 2, Appendix B) for multiple time steps.

ryckaert1977.annotation: The original constraint paper: Lagrange-multiplier dynamics in Cartesian coordinates with constraints exact at every step, a matrix method first, and the iterative SHAKE procedure as the cheaper alternative for large molecules, tested on liquid butane.
ryckaert1977.read_guide: Sections 2 and 3 (Eq. 2.1 to 2.10, 3.3 to 3.5) and Section 5 (Eq. 5.2 to 5.6, cost comparison). Goes with Module 9 (Lagrange multipliers, SHAKE) and the Module 1 timeline.

andersen1983.annotation: RATTLE rebuilds SHAKE on velocity Verlet by using two constraint-force approximations per step, one for positions and one for velocities, so both satisfy the constraints and no previous step is needed.
andersen1983.read_guide: Section II (the inconsistency in Eq. 2.5 and 2.6 and its resolution in 2.7 and 2.8) and Appendix C (the two iteration loops). Goes with Module 9 (RATTLE) and Module 4 (velocity Verlet).

hess1997.annotation: LINCS solves bond constraints by a matrix projection on the old bond directions, inverts the sparse coupling matrix with a short power series, and adds a length correction; it is 3 to 4 times faster than SHAKE and parallelises easily.
hess1997.read_guide: Projection Method and Constrained Leap-Frog Algorithm (Eq. 10 to 19), the Implementation section (Eq. 20 to 22 and the eigenvalue limits), and Table I with Figure 2. Goes with Module 9 (LINCS expansion, tolerance and order).

andersen1980.annotation: Original extended-Lagrangian piston barostat and stochastic-collision thermostat, with proofs that the first gives constant-enthalpy averages and the second canonical averages when the chain is irreducible.
andersen1980.read_guide: Sec. III (Eqs. 3.2 to 3.14 and the piston-mass discussion), Sec. IV (Eqs. 4.1 to 4.12) and Sec. V. Module 8.

parrinello1981.annotation: Extends the extended-Lagrangian barostat so the whole cell matrix is dynamical under any applied stress, generating a constant-enthalpy ensemble, and shows fcc to hcp transitions in model nickel.
parrinello1981.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 2.3 to 2.25) for the cell Lagrangian and equation of motion. Module 8.

berendsen1984.annotation: Introduces weak coupling to a temperature and pressure bath by first-order scaling of velocities and coordinates, tested on 216 SPC waters, and admits the generated ensemble is unproven.
berendsen1984.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 7 to 21), Sec. III algorithm and notes on step order, Sec. IV with Table I and Figs. 1 and 2. Module 8.

nose1984.annotation: Derives constant temperature MD from an extended Hamiltonian with a time-scaling variable, proves it gives the canonical distribution, shows isokinetic constraint methods follow from it, and extends it to constant pressure.
nose1984.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 2.5 to 2.22), Sec. V (choice of g and Q) and Table III. Module 8.

hoover1985.annotation: Hoover's three-page note rewrites Nosé's thermostat without time scaling, proves the canonical density stationary with a Gaussian friction variable, and shows a single oscillator is not ergodic under it.
hoover1985.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 1 to 6), Sec. III (Eqs. 7 and 8, stationarity proof) and Sec. IV with Fig. 1; Module 8, Nosé-Hoover and exercise 2.

martyna1992.annotation: Thermostatting the thermostat variable itself, in a chain, restores canonical sampling for a harmonic oscillator and a free particle where plain Nosé-Hoover fails; the paper gives the chain equations and mass rule.
martyna1992.read_guide: Sec. II (chain equations, mass choice, Hoover holes), Sec. III with Figs. 1 to 3 and 5, Appendix B for masses; Module 8, chains and exercise 2.

martyna1994.annotation: Corrects earlier constant-pressure dynamics so that isotropic and flexible-cell equations of motion generate the isothermal-isobaric ensemble, adds thermostat chains and mass rules, and tests them on a 1D model and C60.
martyna1994.read_guide: Sec. II A (what goes wrong in Hoover's equations, virial argument), II E and II F (chains, masses), Appendix B (virial theorems); Module 8, barostats.

feller1995.annotation: Replaces the deterministic piston of Andersen with a Langevin equation, gives the NPT ensemble without ringing at a suitable collision frequency, and shows that weak-coupling barostats distort volume fluctuations and heat water against octane.
feller1995.read_guide: Sec. I (Eqs. 1 and 2), Sec. II (Eqs. 3 and 4), Figs. 1 to 6, Sec. IV dissipation argument; Module 8, why Berendsen is for equilibration only.

darden1993.annotation: The original particle mesh Ewald letter: direct Ewald sum within a fixed cutoff, reciprocal sum approximated by Lagrange interpolation on a grid and an FFT, giving N log N cost.
darden1993.read_guide: Introduction and Method (Eqs. 2 to 7, error bound) and Table I for the accuracy and cost trade-off with grid spacing and order. Goes with Module 7, Particle-mesh Ewald.

essmann1995.annotation: Recasts particle mesh Ewald as B-spline interpolation of structure factors, so forces are analytic derivatives of a smooth energy, accuracy is tunable independent of size, and dispersion and virial follow.
essmann1995.read_guide: Sec. II (Eqs. 2.1 to 2.5), Sec. IV (Eqs. 4.1 to 4.9), Sec. VI (beta, cutoff, grid, order; Fig. 1, Table II) and Appendix C. Goes with Module 7, Ewald summation and Particle-mesh Ewald.

tironi1995.annotation: Extends the reaction field method to a continuum with salt by solving the linearised Poisson-Boltzmann equation in the cutoff sphere, and shows on 1 M NaCl that it removes cutoff artefacts at no extra cost.
tironi1995.read_guide: Introduction, the Eq. 22 and 23 section with the limits after Eq. 23, and Sec. IV on cutoff artefacts in Fig. 1. Goes with Module 7, Reaction field.

lifson1968.annotation: Founding paper of force-field fitting: one set of energy functions is tuned by weighted least squares to reproduce alkane geometries, vibrational frequencies and enthalpies together, with Urey-Bradley and Lennard-Jones terms.
lifson1968.read_guide: Eqs. 1 to 8 (energy expansion, normal modes), Eqs. 13 to 16 (least-squares fit), and the Urey-Bradley and Lennard-Jones section with Eqs. 30 and 31. For Modules 5 and 6.

weiner1984.annotation: The first AMBER force field: harmonic, cosine, Lennard-Jones and Coulomb energy plus a 10-12 hydrogen-bond term, ESP-fitted charges and 0.5 scaling of 1-4 terms, tested on nucleosides, dipeptides and insulin.
weiner1984.read_guide: General Perspective (Eq. 1), Torsional Parameters, the 1-4 scaling argument in the tetrahydrofuran and methyl ethyl ether section, and the Discussion. For Modules 5 and 6.

bayly1993.annotation: Introduces RESP: a hyperbolic restraint on non-hydrogen charges (weights 0.0005 and 0.001) and a two-stage fit that makes electrostatic-potential charges less conformation-dependent while keeping the polar region accurate.
bayly1993.read_guide: Introduction (why buried charges fail), the Methods equations 5 to 13, the model 3 and two-stage paragraphs, and Tables V and X. For Module 6.

cornell1995.annotation: The second-generation AMBER force field: RESP charges at 6-31G*, Lennard-Jones fitted to liquids, 1-4 factors 1/1.2 (Coulomb) and 1/2 (van der Waals), minimalist dihedrals plus fitted phi and psi terms.
cornell1995.read_guide: General Description of the Model (Eq. 1), the dihedral, van der Waals and electrostatic sections, and the Discussion with Table 13. For Modules 5 and 6.

jorgensen1996.annotation: The original OPLS-AA paper: torsions fitted to RHF/6-31G* scans, charges and Lennard-Jones terms tuned on 34 simulated pure liquids to match heats of vaporisation and densities, with 1,4 factors of one half.
jorgensen1996.read_guide: Computational Methods (Eqs. 1 to 5) and Fitting Procedures for the form and torsion fitting; Liquid Properties for the liquid-based charge fitting. Goes with Modules 5 and 6.

mackerell1998.annotation: The CHARMM22 all-atom protein force field: charges fitted to HF/6-31G(d) water complexes with TIP3P, Urey-Bradley and improper terms added for spectra, and phi and psi tuned against crystal simulations of myoglobin.
mackerell1998.read_guide: Section II (Eq. 1, 1-4 treatment, water model choice, charge fitting with the 1.16 scale factor) and Section IV.a.1 on phi and psi tuning with Tables 5 to 7. Goes with Modules 5 and 6.

ponder2003.annotation: A 2003 review of Class I protein force fields: how Amber, CHARMM and OPLS charges and torsions were derived, what fixed point charges cannot do, polarizable models, and continuum solvent including generalized Born.
ponder2003.read_guide: Section II A to C (pp. 30-39) for fitting of charges, Lennard-Jones and torsions; Table III and Fig. 5 for force-field disagreement; Section III A, D and Table IV for polarization (Modules 5 and 6); Section IV B for generalized Born (Module 15).

oostenbrink2004.annotation: Describes the GROMOS functional form and derives 53A5 and 53A6 by fitting liquids and cyclohexane solvation, then re-tuning only the charges to hydration free enthalpies, because one charge set cannot serve both phases.
oostenbrink2004.read_guide: Functional Form (Eqs. 8 to 19) and the Results and Discussion section on why 53A5 and 53A6 differ, for Modules 5 and 6.

wang2004.annotation: GAFF assigns 35 basic and 22 special atom types from structure, reuses Amber Lennard-Jones values, computes force constants by formulas, uses RESP or AM1-BCC charges and fits torsions last to QM scans; tested only in gas phase.
wang2004.read_guide: Generation of Parameters (atom types, charges, Eqs. 2 to 6, torsion strategy) and the Summary, for Modules 6 and 13; skip the long tables.

nerenberg2018.annotation: A 2018 review of fixed-charge and polarisable force fields that diagnoses over-compact disordered proteins and unfavourable amino-acid hydration, and lists the torsion, water, charge and Bayesian fixes then under way.
nerenberg2018.read_guide: Protein force fields (with Figure 1 on histatin 5) and Small molecule force fields, for Module 6; Future directions for Module 17.

jorgensen1983.annotation: Monte Carlo comparison of six rigid water models at 25 C and 1 atm, giving the TIP3P and TIP4P parameters and showing that 3-site models lose structure beyond the first shell.
jorgensen1983.read_guide: Section II with Tables I and II, Table III (density, energy, compressibility) and Section IV.C on g_OO, for Module 6.

berendsen1987.annotation: Shows that effective pair potentials omit the self-energy of induced dipoles, derives E_pol = (mu - mu0)^2 / 2 alpha and refits SPC to get SPC/E, improving density and diffusion.
berendsen1987.read_guide: Equations 13 to 17 and page 3 (Table I, SPC/E definition) for the missing-term box in Module 6.

kirkwood1935.annotation: Introduces coupling parameters that switch one molecule's interactions on, giving the chemical potential as an integral over the mean interaction energy, and defines the potential of mean force with its mean-force property.
kirkwood1935.read_guide: Section II, Eqs. 7-22 and 26-28 (printed pages 301-304); skip Sections IV-V. Goes with Module 13 (thermodynamic integration) and Modules 3 and 12 (potential of mean force).

zwanzig1954.annotation: Derives the exact identity exp(-beta Delta A) = <exp(-beta Delta U)> over the reference ensemble and its high-temperature cumulant series, then applies the first-order term to argon and nitrogen.
zwanzig1954.read_guide: Section II, Eqs. 2-16 (printed pages 1421-1422): the identity and the cumulant expansion; skip the rest. Goes with Module 13 (free-energy perturbation).

bennett1976.annotation: Derives the optimal two-ensemble acceptance ratio estimator with a Fermi function and a self-consistent shift, shows it beats one-sided perturbation by large factors, and adds an interpolation method for poor overlap.
bennett1976.read_guide: Section II (Eqs. 2-12) for the BAR estimator and Section IV (Eqs. 22-24) for its relation to perturbation, the Gibbs-Bogoliubov bound and integration. Goes with Module 13 (BAR) and Module 12 (MBAR).

torrie1977.annotation: Introduces umbrella sampling: Monte Carlo with an arbitrary weight on the energy difference, exact reweighting to unbiased averages, and overlapping runs, tested by computing Lennard-Jones free energies.
torrie1977.read_guide: Section 2 (Eqs. 1-7, pages 188-190), the trial-and-error weights discussion (page 198) and the block-error remark (page 197). Goes with Module 12 (umbrella sampling and unbiasing).

flyvbjerg1989.annotation: Original description of blocking: repeatedly halving a correlated series leaves the mean and its variance unchanged and makes the naive error estimate rise to a plateau, giving the true error with a known uncertainty.
flyvbjerg1989.read_guide: Sections II to IV (Eqs. 5, 14, 20-28), then Sec. VII with Figs. 2-4 and Sec. VIII with Table I, for Module 11.

beutler1994.annotation: Introduces soft-core Lennard-Jones and Coulomb potentials for creating or removing atoms: a squared lambda shift in the denominator removes the divergence of the lambda derivative and the MD time-step instability.
beutler1994.read_guide: Section 2 (Fig. 1), Section 3 (Eqs. 7-8), Section 4 (Eq. 9, Figs. 2-3) and Appendix A (n >= 4 criterion), for Module 13.

hess2000.annotation: Proves that PCA of high-dimensional random diffusion gives cosine components with eigenvalues falling as 1/k^2, so short protein simulations give cosine-like leading modes that reflect poor sampling, not collective motion.
hess2000.read_guide: Analysis of random diffusion (Eqs. 1-27), Validation (Figs. 1-4), the OMPf and HPr examples and the Discussion, for Module 11.

hess2002.annotation: Defines the cosine content and a covariance-matrix overlap, tests them on 40 ns protein runs and a harmonic diffusion model, and concludes that cosine content is only a negative indicator of convergence.
hess2002.read_guide: Section II (Eqs. 1-12, Fig. 8), Section V (Figs. 10-11) and the Discussion, for Module 11.

boresch2003.annotation: Derives the exact analytic free energy of releasing six harmonic restraints (one distance, two angles, three dihedrals), enabling converged double-decoupling binding free energies with a defined standard state, and tests it on lysozyme and tyrosine models.
boresch2003.read_guide: Section 2.1 (eq 7-14, Figure 2) and Section 2.2 (eq 26-32), then Table 5 and Section 5.3 on the restraint free energy versus entropy loss. For Module 13.

yeh2004.annotation: Shows that periodic images make simulated diffusion coefficients too small by an amount proportional to 1/L, derives the correction 2.837 kT/(6 pi eta L) for cubic boxes and verifies it on water and simple fluids.
yeh2004.read_guide: Section II (eq 9-12 and the extrapolation advice), Section III with Table 1 and Figure 2, and the electrostatic caveat in the conclusions. For Module 11.

sugita1999.annotation: The original molecular dynamics version of temperature replica exchange: velocity rescaling by the square root of the temperature ratio, Metropolis swaps on potential energy, tested on gas-phase Met-enkephalin with 8 replicas and reweighting.
sugita1999.read_guide: Section 2 (Eqs. 5-17: permutation labels, momentum rescaling, acceptance criterion) and Section 3 (Table 1, the three checks for a good ladder, Figs. 3 and 5) for module 14.

isralewitz2001.annotation: Review of steered MD in the context of AFM force spectroscopy: pulling protocols (moving spring, constant force), avidin-biotin and titin I27 case studies, and nonequilibrium analysis by Jarzynski and PMF reconstruction.
isralewitz2001.read_guide: Pages 4-6 (variations of steering forces, analysis of SMD) for module 14 steered MD; Fig. 1 and the avidin-biotin section for the loading-rate idea; the 41 pN = 1 kBT remark on page 1.

taketomi1975.annotation: The founding structure-based model: a 49-unit chain on a square lattice where only native-contact pairs attract, sampled by Metropolis Monte Carlo, showing that specific interactions make folding all-or-none.
taketomi1975.read_guide: Section I (three specificities, Fig. 1) and Section III (Figs. 6, 8, 11, case B). Module 15, structure-based models.

ermak1978.annotation: Derives the Brownian dynamics step from the Fokker-Planck and Langevin equations, with diffusion tensor, drift term and correlated noise for hydrodynamic interactions, tested on dimers and trimers.
ermak1978.read_guide: Sections II and III (Eqs. 2 to 5, 14) for the overdamped step and noise; Section IV (Eqs. 15 to 20) for hydrodynamics. Modules 8 and 15.

still1990.annotation: Defines the GB/SA continuum model for molecular mechanics: Born plus Coulomb interpolated by f_GB, numerically computed Born radii and a surface-area term, validated against free energy perturbation.
still1990.read_guide: The whole two-page communication: Eqs. 3 to 5, the f_GB limits paragraph, Table I. Module 15, implicit solvent.

miyazawa1996.annotation: Re-derives residue-pair contact energies from 1168 crystal structures with a lattice quasi-chemical model, adds a repulsive packing term, and shows the combination ranks native folds lowest in threading.
miyazawa1996.read_guide: Methods (Eqs. 14 to 31) and Table 3; Discussion on units and potentials of mean force. Module 15, statistical contact potentials.

clementi2000.annotation: Introduces the C-alpha Go Hamiltonian with 12-10 native contacts and shows that on five small proteins native topology alone reproduces experimental transition states and most intermediates, but not barrier heights.
clementi2000.read_guide: Appendix (Eq. A1, parameters, contact definition, WHAM); phi-value Eqs 1-5; CI2, SH3 and CheY results (Figs 1, 2, 9, 10). For Module 15.

onufriev2004.annotation: Replaces the Hawkins-Cramer-Truhlar effective Born radius with a tanh-rescaled burial function (GB-OBC, two parameter sets), removing most of the bias of GB toward compact native structures relative to Poisson-Boltzmann.
onufriev2004.read_guide: Eqs 1-8, Figs 1-3 and Table I, then Methods on protocol and parameter sets. For Module 15.

hanggi1990.annotation: Authoritative review of reaction-rate theory: transition-state theory, Kramers' rates at weak, moderate and strong friction, the turnover, Grote-Hynes memory friction, mean first-passage times and reactive-flux numerics, with all prefactors derived.
hanggi1990.read_guide: Sections III.A, III.C, IV.A to IV.E, IV.G, VI.A, VI.B and X (journal pp. 261 to 274, 278, 286 to 289, 323 to 324) for Module 16; Section VII.C.1 for the first-passage exercises.

behler2007.annotation: Introduces the atom-by-atom neural-network potential: symmetry functions describe each atom's neighbourhood within a cutoff, identical subnets give atomic energies that sum to the total, demonstrated on bulk silicon against DFT.
behler2007.read_guide: Whole 4-page Letter: Eqs. 2-5 (atomic energy sum, cutoff, radial and angular symmetry functions) and the silicon results on page 3-4; goes with Module 17.

jo2008.annotation: Describes the first web interface that builds CHARMM inputs: PDB reading, solvation and ions, a standard equilibration setup, membranes, Poisson-Boltzmann and implicit solvent modules, with its default settings.
jo2008.read_guide: PDB Reader, Solvator (Eq. 1 for ion numbers) and Quick MD Simulator sections, pages 2-4; goes with Module 10 (setup) and Module 7 (PME settings).

abraham2015.annotation: Software paper for GROMACS 5: simulation capabilities, cluster-pair Verlet lists, SIMD and GPU offload, domain decomposition, triclinic boxes, Lennard-Jones PME, with benchmarks on membrane proteins.
abraham2015.read_guide: Sections 2 (capabilities), 3 (Verlet scheme, boxes, PME) and 5 with Figs. 5-6; goes with Modules 7, 9 and 10.

thompson2022.annotation: Overview of LAMMPS for materials: spatial decomposition, neighbour lists, PPPM, flexible style-based design, GPU and scaling results, many-body, coarse-grained and machine-learned potentials, units and multi-replica methods.
thompson2022.read_guide: Sections 3.3 and 3.4 (neighbour lists, PPPM), 6.3 (machine-learned potentials), 6.6 and 6.7 (replica methods, PLUMED, unit styles); goes with Modules 7, 14 and 17.

horn2004.annotation: TIP4P-Ew re-fits TIP4P to density and enthalpy of vaporisation over 235 to 400 K with Ewald electrostatics, shows a density maximum near 274 K, and documents the vaporisation corrections.
horn2004.read_guide: Methods A-D and E.4 (Eqs. 19-26), Tables I, V, VI for Module 6; Appendix for the virtual M site in Module 9.

abascal2005.annotation: TIP4P/2005 refits the TIP4P form to the density maximum, ice densities and ice III stability, and shows the trade-off with melting point and dielectric constant.
abascal2005.read_guide: Sec. III B, Tables I to III, Sec. IV G and Conclusions for Module 6 water models.

darve2001.annotation: Derives the exact free-energy derivative as the mean instantaneous force plus a geometric term, in constrained or free runs, and names the adaptive force method that grew into ABF.
darve2001.read_guide: Introduction, Eq. 11 and Eq. 35 with discussion, and the Discussion section (journal page 9178) for the adaptive force idea. Goes with Module 14, and Modules 3 and 12.

hamelberg2004.annotation: Introduces the smooth boost (E - V)^2/(alpha + E - V) below a threshold, reweights by exp(beta dV), and tests it on alanine peptides in implicit solvent with the boost on dihedral terms only.
hamelberg2004.read_guide: Theory (Eq. 1 to 10, Fig. 2 and 3), parameter advice alpha near E - V_min, and the dihedral-only version (Eq. 12 to 14). Goes with Module 14.

noid2008.annotation: Defines consistency between atomistic and coarse-grained ensembles, shows the exact CG potential is the many-body potential of mean force, and proves that force matching minimises a functional uniquely minimised by its mean force.
noid2008.read_guide: Section II D-E (Eqs. 18-28), Section III A (Eqs. 33-39) and the seven-step recipe in Section IV; for Module 15 and Modules 17-18.

shell2008.annotation: Shows that the relative entropy between a target and a model ensemble is a log-likelihood measure whose minimum, for a coarse-grained model, is the projected free energy surface, and gives update rules for parameters.
shell2008.read_guide: Sections II and III (Eqs. 1-12, 16-17, 21-22); the water case study can be skipped; for the relative-entropy bullet of Module 15.

noid2013.annotation: A 2013 survey of top-down, native-structure-based and bottom-up coarse-graining, built around the many-body potential of mean force, with the open problems of mapping, representability and transferability.
noid2013.read_guide: Sections III and V (philosophies, PMF), VII A-B (Boltzmann inversion, relative entropy, MS-CG) and IX D-E (representability, transferability); for Module 15.

prinz2011.annotation: Reviews Markov state models of molecular kinetics: transfer operator spectrum, an error bound showing non-metastable states near barriers help, a reversible estimator, uncertainties, and the Chapman-Kolmogorov validation test.
prinz2011.read_guide: Sec. II B (Eqs. 5-19, implied time scales), Sec. III C-E (error bound, Figs. 5-8), Sec. IV D-F (Eq. 53, Algorithm 1, Chapman-Kolmogorov test Eqs. 60-65) for Module 16.
